title: Coordinate online task operations through Work Origin
scope: Implement the lightweight online Work Origin client in shared core/standalone creation and mutation operations and expose aligned behavior through CLI and MCP. Explicit project enrollment assigns stable outask_origin_uuid task identities while retaining numeric IDs, existing records and unknown fields. Register each independent clone/worktree as outask_client using hostname plus a server-assigned numeric suffix; reconnecting the same copy preserves its identity, while independent copies and coincident hostnames must not share authority accidentally. Coordinate creation, taking ownership, changes, completion and archival across every retained status/store, checking current ownership and revisions. Reject unintended edits to another client's work and stale changes; require explicit confirmation tied to the concrete operation and expected state for force, including destructive replacement of an occupied ID. Recover safely from lost replies and local write failures without duplicate tasks or repeat application. Keep server traffic limited to coordination data; local JSON/Git retain full task content. Preserve unchanged non-coordinated task formats, numeric allocation, statuses, lists, outputs and network-free operation. Update affected user/contributor contracts and pass required checks. Offline reconciliation, server implementation/installation/systemd management and Git-hook integration are excluded and belong to subsequent delivery tasks. Follow docs/releases.md: synchronization-related implementation is scheduled only after unrelated active tasks are delivered and ships only in Outask 2.0.0 or later, never in a 1.x release. Refresh unrelated backlog readiness before starting; inherited dependencies enforce the current ordering.
acceptance: Against a real Outask Server, two independent project directories concurrently create tasks with distinct positive safe-integer numeric IDs and outask_origin_uuid values; project identity isolates unrelated projects and all retained IDs remain occupied.

Independent clones/worktrees register distinct outask_client identifiers with atomically allocated hostname-based suffixes. Reconnection retains the same client; hostnames alone do not grant another client's authority. Coordination enrollment is explicit and preserves existing task fields and records.

Two clients attempting to take the same task concurrently yield one successful owner and a clear conflict for the other. Ordinary edits, completion, archival and other mutations reject conflicting ownership or stale state across all retained statuses, including custom statuses.

CLI and MCP force flows require explicit confirmation of a concrete operation, affected task, owner, expected state and destructive consequences. Changed state invalidates prior confirmation; no permanent blanket force permission is introduced. An occupied numeric ID can be explicitly replaced, never duplicated within the final store.

Lost replies and retries do not create an additional task or apply an operation twice. Exercise local failure after server authorization and recovery without silently overwriting another client's work. Network waits do not hold the local writer lock; ordinary validation and local write coordination still apply.

Without configured Work Origin, regression checks demonstrate unchanged task fields/bytes, numeric ID allocation, statuses, lists and command outputs, with no coordination requests, added fields or installed-server dependency.

Exercise actual shared operations, standalone/CLI and MCP boundaries against the runnable server using two independent directories. Document enrollment, online conflicts, confirmation and recovery; keep public help/contracts aligned and pass required CI. Fixtures alone do not satisfy real-server acceptance.

Follow docs/releases.md: synchronization-related implementation is scheduled only after unrelated active tasks are delivered and ships only in Outask 2.0.0 or later, never in a 1.x release. Refresh unrelated backlog readiness before starting; inherited dependencies enforce the current ordering.

title: Continue task work offline and reconcile pending changes
scope: Continue coordinated Outask task work when Work Origin is unreachable and reconcile it after reconnecting. Maintain a durable local queue outside Git-tracked project files. Support offline creation, taking ownership, edits, completion and archival while preserving full task content in local JSON/Git. Create stable outask_origin_uuid identities immediately; consume non-overlapping client-allocated numeric ID blocks while valid, then allow provisional numeric IDs without blocking creation. Explicitly show unconfirmed operations and ownership. Known foreign ownership requires explicitly confirmed force; taking a task last known to be free is provisional. Reconcile operations in bounded batches, automatically confirming compatible changes and retaining conflicts for user resolution without silently discarding work. Require confirmation for renumbering and update known structural references without silently rewriting arbitrary text, external references or Git branch names. Reconfirm ownership and ID allocations after the coordinator is rebuilt from a selected Git state on another host without transferring its database. Detect changes made by editors or older clients during reconciliation. Keep core/standalone, CLI and MCP behavior aligned, document offline/recovery scenarios and preserve unchanged operation for projects without configured coordination. Server implementation, service installation/lifecycle and Git-hook changes are excluded. Follow docs/releases.md: synchronization-related implementation is scheduled only after unrelated active tasks are delivered and ships only in Outask 2.0.0 or later, never in a 1.x release. Refresh unrelated backlog readiness before starting; inherited dependencies enforce the current ordering.
acceptance: Two disconnected clients continue creating, taking, editing, closing and archiving tasks. New tasks immediately receive outask_origin_uuid; UUID identity survives reconciliation and numeric renumbering. Local task work remains readable and persisted before confirmation.

Numeric IDs from valid client blocks do not overlap across clients. Exhausted or unavailable blocks allow provisional numeric IDs and clearly expose their unconfirmed state rather than blocking creation. After server reconstruction, prior blocks are not assumed valid without reconfirmation.

Changes to tasks known to belong to another client require explicit force confirmation. Offline taking of a task last known to be free is marked provisional; simultaneous offline claims are detected during reconciliation. Offline completion or status changes do not silently assert server confirmation.

Upon reconnecting, compatible operations are confirmed automatically in bounded batches. Conflicting ownership, stale changes, numeric collisions and forced edits are presented for explicit resolution; local work is not silently overwritten, dropped or declared accepted.

Renumbering shows affected tasks/references and requires confirmation, preserving outask_origin_uuid. Known structural references such as blockers are updated consistently and validated; arbitrary task text, external links and Git branch names are not silently rewritten. Explicitly confirmed destructive force remains tied to the concrete operation and expected state.

A durable local queue survives client restart, lost replies and interrupted reconciliation without duplicate task creation or repeated operation application. Queue, credentials and client identity remain outside Git-tracked project files; network waits do not hold local writer locks.

Against a real coordinator rebuilt on another host from an agreed Git snapshot without a database transfer, previously connected clients preserve pending work, reconfirm ownership and allocations, and reconcile their operations without silently reusing obsolete authority.

Reconciliation detects manual/editor and older-client changes and offers ordinary or explicitly confirmed forced resolution. Server-free projects retain their existing fields, numeric allocation, statuses, lists, command behavior and absence of network requests.

Verify two independent project directories and actual Outask Server through affected core/standalone, CLI and MCP boundaries, covering disconnect/reconnect, concurrent offline work, provisional-ID collisions, client restart, repeated sync and coordinator reconstruction. Document the behavior and pass required CI; mocked-server checks alone do not satisfy integrated acceptance.

Follow docs/releases.md: synchronization-related implementation is scheduled only after unrelated active tasks are delivered and ships only in Outask 2.0.0 or later, never in a 1.x release. Refresh unrelated backlog readiness before starting; inherited dependencies enforce the current ordering.

title: Configure Work Origin connections and manage the Linux server service
scope: Provide outask origin up/down/status as configuration and wrappers around standard systemd lifecycle commands, keeping the Linux Outask Server implementation in its separate project/package. Check installed Outask, the server component, runtime dependencies, service configuration and access to registered server-side project checkouts. When absent, offer explicit installation of the separate server package. Register multiple projects with one system service operating outside project directories. Ask for the published project address, keep bind and published addresses distinct, and save the shared project binding without automatic Git commits or publication. Support local per-project address overrides and explicitly selected network profiles for loopback, LAN and Internet endpoints; retain credentials outside committed files. Diagnose service/connectivity failures and point users to journald. Remote coordinator clients remain usable on supported non-Linux platforms; server installation/start is Linux-only. Preserve unchanged operation without configured coordination. Update documentation and verify the real service. Server implementation, offline reconciliation, NAT/port forwarding, DNS setup and Git-hook changes are excluded. Follow docs/releases.md: synchronization-related implementation is scheduled after unrelated active tasks and is released only in Outask 2.0.0 or later.
acceptance: On Linux, origin up checks prerequisites, obtains explicit authorization for any installation or required system privileges, registers the selected project and starts the standard system service. systemctl can independently start/stop/restart/report that same service; origin wrappers do not create a second process manager.

One service coordinates multiple registered projects outside their checkout directories. Installed Outask and accessible project checkouts are required. Failure to access one registered project blocks that project's coordination without stopping the others.

Bind and published addresses are separately configurable. The published address is requested from the user and saved to the shared project configuration; no automatic commit, push, DNS or port-forwarding change occurs.

After receiving shared configuration through Git, another environment knows the project origin address. Local user configuration overrides addresses per stable project identity and selected network profile, including loopback, LAN and public endpoints.
Different endpoint addresses are checked for the intended project identity, not trusted solely by address or hostname. Credentials are neither committed nor exposed in logs.

origin down warns that the shared service serves all registered projects before stopping it, preserving project registrations and bindings. status reports service state and the selected project's connection state; diagnostics include journalctl usage.
Remote-origin connection works on supported Linux/macOS/Windows clients; server installation and service lifecycle actions are explicitly limited to Linux.

title: Integrate Work Origin checks with existing Git hooks
scope: Extend existing outask hook --install/--remove with optional Work Origin checks before Git publication, retaining current working-tree JSON validation before commit. Preserve existing user hooks/checks and provide safe integration/removal in shared hook locations. Do not perform implicit synchronization, task writes, renumbering, staging, commits or publication. Preserve existing no-origin behavior, document supported platforms/limitations and verify real clone/worktree scenarios. Remote Git enforcement and repository administration are excluded. Hooks do not silently synchronize, renumber, edit tasks, stage data, create commits or publish. Manual/editor or older-client changes are detected against available coordination state without claiming detection of unknown remote offline work.

Projects without configured origin retain their prior task behavior and hook checks. title: Wait for npm registry visibility before verifying publication
scope: Correct the reproduced Outask v1.7 publication failure in scripts/npm-release.mjs: npm publish succeeded through trusted publishing and reported asynchronous processing, but the immediate metadata read could not yet see 1.7.0 and incorrectly reported an integrity mismatch. After an accepted publication, use bounded read-only retries for visibility of the exact approved package version and its intended dist-tag, then verify the published integrity against the already accepted artifact. Distinguish a not-yet-visible version/tag, transient registry failures, an actual immutable integrity mismatch and authentication/publication rejection. Preserve owner-merged release approval, existing-version safeguards, bootstrap behavior and stable/prerelease tag rules. Retry metadata reads only; never repeat npm publish inside the wait or automatically replace/delete/retag a published version. Keep the change small and within the existing publication helper and its focused tests.
acceptance: A deterministic registry fixture initially hides a successfully accepted version and/or serves the old intended dist-tag, then exposes the approved integrity and tag; verification eventually passes after bounded read retries with exactly one publish invocation.

Published version metadata containing a different integrity fails as an actual immutable-artifact mismatch. The helper never overwrites, deletes or retags that version, and authentication or rejected-publish failures retain actionable diagnostics rather than being reported as propagation delay.

The wait has a finite deadline/retry budget. If the expected version or dist-tag never becomes visible, it exits nonzero with the package/version, last observed state and clear pending-visibility or registry-error wording; absence is not described as a confirmed integrity mismatch. Transient registry failures stay within the same bound.

A rerun against an already visible approved version and intended dist-tag succeeds without invoking npm publish. Existing-version collision checks, initial-registry bootstrap handoff and stable/prerelease latest/next selection retain their contracts.

Focused tests cover delayed version visibility, delayed tag visibility, timeout, transient registry failure, real integrity mismatch and publish rejection using controlled responses and deterministic timing; they perform no real npm publication. Required local checks pass, and contributor guidance is updated only if the recovery procedure changes.

values.goal: Publish approved Outask releases reliably while preserving immutable package integrity and owner approval.

values.result: A successful publication waits for public visibility and completes verification automatically; real mismatches and expired waits still fail clearly.
values.verification: Run controlled publication scenarios with one accepted publish and delayed metadata/tag responses; observe eventual success, bounded timeout and correct hard-failure diagnostics without repeat publication.

title: Ship a project HTTP API command with project environment configuration and optional token authentication
scope: Make the existing outask http command a supported installed command for serving one selected project's read-only HTTP API. Ship the adapter in npm packages and release archives, expose discoverable help, and preserve current-directory, positional path, --project-path, registered --project, --config and --schema-path selection. Load only the selected project's root .env for API settings, even when invoked elsewhere, with precedence CLI options > process environment > project .env > defaults. Support --port/TASKS_HTTP_PORT and --host/TASKS_HTTP_HOST; retain default port 4318, port 0 for an available port, and default host 127.0.0.1, with explicit 0.0.0.0 binding for remote clients. Make TASKS_HTTP_TOKEN optional: absent or empty means open access; a configured nonempty valid token requires Authorization: Bearer authentication. Open mode permits any browser origin; protected mode retains explicit --allow-origin restrictions and preflight support. Preserve shared read routes, results, boundaries and freshness while updating owning contracts and operator documentation. HTTPS deployment, system-service installation, HTTP mutations and Work Origin coordination are outside scope.
acceptance: From an installed npm package and release archive, outask http starts without a source checkout or manual dependency setup; outask --help and outask http --help discover the command and its options. Preserve the permanent tasks command alias and applicable project/schema selectors.

Resolve the project before loading its root .env; invocation from another directory reads the selected project's file, never a caller or ancestor project's file. Missing .env is allowed. Parse settings as data without executing shell commands; unrelated keys do not alter other Outask commands. Configuration precedence is CLI > process environment > project .env > defaults, including explicitly empty token settings.

--port and TASKS_HTTP_PORT select the port; default is 4318 and 0 requests an available port. --host and TASKS_HTTP_HOST select the listen address; default is 127.0.0.1 and explicit 0.0.0.0 supports connections from other machines. Invalid configuration and occupied ports fail clearly without silently selecting another port. Startup reports the actual listen address/port and authentication mode without revealing secrets.

Missing or empty TASKS_HTTP_TOKEN enables reads without credentials. A nonempty token preserves the existing 32–512 URL-safe-character contract and requires Bearer authentication for all data routes: correct token succeeds and missing, malformed or incorrect credentials receive 401. Invalid configured tokens stop startup rather than falling back to open access. Token values are not printed in help, startup output, logs or errors; restart applies token changes and invalidates the old token.

Open mode permits requests from any browser origin, with working CORS/preflight and no cookie credentials. Protected mode preserves exact repeatable --allow-origin configuration, rejects disallowed origins and requires the token on actual reads; valid preflight can omit it and never exposes task data.

One process remains bound to one startup-selected project/schema; requests cannot switch project, registry or schema. Separate processes can serve two projects on distinct ports with independent .env settings and tokens. Existing HTTP reads, shared JSON shapes, pagination, response limits, filesystem boundaries and visibility of subsequent CLI/manual JSON changes remain aligned; HTTP writes remain unavailable.

Verify actual installed-command startup from npm and archive payloads, independent projects and environment files, configuration precedence, open/protected requests, token replacement after restart, CORS, remote binding, invalid/occupied ports, and stop/restart releasing the port. Run focused CLI/HTTP/packaging regression checks and applicable repository checks.

Detect the running installation and update it through its owning mechanism: reuse the existing release updater for managed archives on Linux, macOS and Windows, and delegate global npm installations to npm in the correct installation context. Add meaningful dedicated automated update and --check coverage for all supported native operating systems and installation contexts: newer/current versions, non-mutating checks, failed network/download/registry/permissions where applicable, custom paths/prefixes, multiple installations, data preservation and guidance-only contexts. Reuse existing archive/npm lifecycle fixtures and gates where suitable.

Configure the dedicated update/check automated suite to run only for explicit regression verification and release verification, not ordinary fast/unit checks or routine non-regression CI. Document its invocation and verify both gate inclusion and exclusion; retain applicable existing repository acceptance requirements.

Update CLI help and owning installation/npm/shared-contract documentation with short commands, mechanism selection, check behavior, guidance-only contexts and session handling. Demonstrate commands against installed archive/npm artifacts and record native-platform regression/release evidence under the repository delivery policy.
